name: Pepper Anthracnose (Ripe Fruit Rot)
description: A fungal disease causing sunken lesions on pepper fruits, particularly on ripening fruits. It is one of the most important post-harvest diseases of pepper in tropical regions, causing significant fruit loss.
symptoms: Circular sunken water-soaked lesions on fruit
Lesions turning tan with dark margins
Pink to orange spore masses in lesion centers
Leaf and stem lesions in severe infections
causes: Colletotrichum capsici and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides fungi
Extended wet periods during fruit ripening
Continuous pepper cultivation with infected debris
treatments: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb preventively
Spray azoxystrobin at flowering and fruit set stages
Remove and destroy infected fruits promptly
Apply copper-based fungicides for organic production
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
Use drip irrigation to keep fruit dry
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
Space plants for good air circulation
